name: Velasquez
lede: Velasquez is a deep, wine-colored plum in a 1930 color atlas, spelled without the accent of the Spanish painter it presumably honors.

sections.title: A name in an atlas
sections.body:
Our library takes the color from the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930, which dates the name to 1925 and places it on plate 54 [1]. No book we hold says who coined it or why [1]. The name presumably recalls Diego Velázquez, but that is our inference and the origin is undocumented [1]. The spelling follows the atlas.

The painter is a poor guide to the color. Ball writes that Velázquez may have used Vandyke brown, a brown quite unlike this plum [2]. The swatch is a dark red-purple; its nearest named neighbors are [[byzantium]] at 8.8 units and [[dahlia-purple]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color near this swatch appears in 8 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 0.03 per cent, rarer than 70 per cent of named colors [3]. The earliest dated match is 1850, in a painting by Nicaise de Keyser, 80 years before the atlas [3]. With 8 cases, in photographs of aged paintings, this tells us only that the color is scarce [3].
